cards.text: Jesus, God's Son, just finished telling a story about a nobleman who goes away to become king (Luke 19:11-27). Now He goes on ahead, going up to Jerusalem. Near Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, He sends out two of His disciples.

cards.question: Jesus sends two disciples into the village ahead. What does He say they'll find tied up there?
Jesus tells the two disciples that no one has ever sat on this colt.

cards.text: Jesus tells them to untie it and bring it to Him. He even gets them ready for the awkward moment when somebody asks, “Why are you untying it?”

cards.question: If anyone asks the two disciples why they're untying the colt, what does Jesus tell them to say?

answers.text: We will bring it back soon

cards.text: So the two head out, and they find it just as Jesus had told them. Friend, when MY phone says “You have arrived,” I'm staring at an empty parking lot.

cards.question: As the disciples are untying the colt, its ___ ask them why they're untying it.
When the owners ask why, the two disciples answer with the line Jesus gave them: The Lord needs it.

cards.text: They lead the colt to Jesus. But before anybody climbs on, the disciples get it ready for Him.

cards.question: Before they put Jesus on the colt, what do the disciples throw over it?

cards.text: As Jesus rides along, the people spread their cloaks on the road. Friend, those cloaks just got PROMOTED. Yesterday they were jackets, today they're a red carpet.

As Jesus approaches the descent from the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of disciples starts praising God joyfully in a loud voice. And I mean LOUD, friend, like a stadium when the home team scores.

cards.question: The whole crowd of disciples is praising God joyfully as Jesus approaches the descent from the Mount of Olives. What are they praising Him for?

answers.text: All the miracles they had seen

cards.text: They shout, “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!”
But some of the Pharisees, a group of strict religious teachers, are in the crowd, and they've got a request for Jesus.

cards.question: Some Pharisees in the crowd call Jesus Teacher and ask Him to ___ His disciples.

cards.text: The Pharisees want the volume turned DOWN. Jesus doesn't touch the knob. He answers them right there in the middle of all that noise, and I bet they did NOT see this one coming.

cards.question: Jesus tells the Pharisees that if His disciples remain silent, something else will cry out. What is it?

cards.text: All that praise on the road, and now Jesus comes near Jerusalem. He sees the city.

cards.question: As Jesus approaches Jerusalem and sees the city, He ___ over it.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, “If only you had known on this day what would bring you peace!” The crowd is shouting about peace in heaven, and Jesus is talking about the peace this city missed.

cards.question: Jesus says that what would bring Jerusalem peace is now hidden from its eyes.

cards.text: Then Jesus looks ahead. He says the days will come when the city's enemies will barricade it, surround it and hem it in on every side.

cards.question: Jesus says the city's enemies will surround Jerusalem but leave its walls standing.
Why does Jesus say all this will come on Jerusalem?

answers.text: It did not recognize God's visit
It did not keep the Sabbath
It made peace with its enemies

findings.problem: The question relies on card 7 to explain who 'the owners' are and what they are asking 'why' about. It should say that the colt's owners are asking why the disciples are untying it, so the question is understandable when the earlier card is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This is not the opening card, but it has three sentences: one about the Pharisees, one about Jesus not touching the knob, and one about Him answering them.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Verse 44 is reduced to a false statement about leaving the walls standing. The walkthrough never clearly tells that the enemies will level Jerusalem and the children within its walls, or that they will not leave one stone on another. Those are central details of Jesus's warning, not minor details that can be dropped.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: 'All this' points back to events described on earlier cards without saying what they are. The question needs to identify the coming destruction of Jerusalem so it stands on its own.
